messages:
Maya: quick sync — planning an accelerator onramp sprint next week. goal: get 3 pilot customers onto the new GPU-backed model variants with minimal customer friction. thoughts on top risks?
Liam: main risk is incompatible tokenization / request shapes across older pinned versions. if we route by model name alone some customers will suddenly see different outputs.
Eva: agreed. runtime also needs a compatibility shim for KV cache layout differences. can do a shim that translates older KV keys to the new layout at serve-time, but it costs ~8% latency for those requests.
Sam: for pilot customers we can offer an opt-in canary route so they only get switched if they accept the small latency bump. that avoids surprise for PLG users.
Ali: customers will push back on any visible latency regression. can we offer a migration window where we run A/B for 2 weeks and provide cost offsets?
Maya: launch criteria proposal: (1) benchmark parity on quality (no >=5% regression on customer prompts), (2) tail latency < 250ms p95 for non-shim traffic, (3) compatibility shim available as fallback for pinned routes, (4) customer opt-ins documented and a rollback path.
Liam: technically we can enforce (2) by limiting shard sizes for shimmed traffic. also want a metric: % of requests hitting shim — if >10% we should freeze rollout.
Eva: can we get a quick perf run? I can spin up a microbench for the variant + shim. what token lengths to measure?
Maya: use 16/64/512 buckets (50/30/20 split) to reflect production. include streaming and non-streaming.
Sam: note for solutions: some customers will want a gracepath exemption — keep pinned old model for 90 days. we'll need a formal exemption policy and SLA note.
Ali: propose customers requesting exemption must sign an acceptance of temporary cost pass-through and a migration plan. otherwise we can't keep pinned versions indefinitely.
Maya: agreed. also need eval pass criteria: run customer prompt set through both old and new variants; automatic scoring + human spot-check for subtle hallucination increases.
Liam: operationally, we should add a routing policy: route to new variant by default, fallback to pinned when shim fails or latency > 500ms. add a feature flag to control the policy per-tenant.
Eva: feature flag + staged rollout implemented. one ask: expose a "compat-shim-enabled" token in trace logs so we can query post-rollout.
Maya: good call. Sam, can you draft a one-page playbook for customer-facing folks with opt-in instructions, rollback steps, and comm templates?
Sam: will do. ETA Tue. includes script for creating a canary route and the postgres query to list shimmed requests.
Maya: quick example command Sam can include:
```
# create canary route for tenant-123
redwood routes create --tenant tenant-123 --model rdx-accelerator-v1 --canary 10% --fallback pinned:rtx-old
```
Liam: small nit: name fallback as explicit model version to avoid ambiguity.
Ali: what about billing? if we serve on accelerator variant, costs will be higher. need clear pricing note in the playbook. customers must approve cost delta.
Maya: include price multiplier and opt-in checkbox. also include comm line: "we'll monitor quality and latency and will reach out if any regression is detected."
Eva: I'll run perf tests tonight and post numbers. if shim pushes p95 > 450ms for 512 tokens we shouldn't enable shim by default.
Maya: agreed. final decision timeline: perf numbers in by EOD tomorrow, Sam playbook Tue, then we open pilot signups Wed. any objections?
Liam: none from eng-platform.
Eva: no objections.
Sam: sounds good.
Ali: fine from CS.
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: onramp-shim-v1 -> staging at 1717555605
Maya: great — thanks team, will follow up with a short RFC summarizing criteria and rollout plan.
